title: Observability-Driven Traffic Shaping and Fallbacks Playbook
author: Daniel Park
content:
Summary:
This playbook documents a standardized, observability-driven approach to shaping incoming traffic and executing graceful fallbacks when platform-level capacity constraints or downstream regressions are detected. It combines detection rules, traffic control policies, degradation tiers, and automated fallback actions so product teams can keep user-visible features running with predictable SLO impact.

Scope:
- Applies to Redwood platform ingress services and internal service-to-service gateways (API edge, request-router, model-proxy).
- Covers automated and manual actions for transient and sustained incidents.
- Does NOT replace service-level runbooks for application bugs (but coordinates with them).

Goals and acceptance criteria:
- Keep core API availability >= 99.95% during partial degradation events.
- Bound p95 latency increase to no more than 2x baseline under Tier 1 degradation for 15 minutes.
- Ensure token-cost-sensitive endpoints have an automated degradation path to reduce per-token spend by >= 30% within 5 minutes of trigger.

Ownership and escalation:
- Primary owner: Platform Traffic & Resilience team (eng-platform).
- Pager: platform-sre@redwood.com for sev2+, platform-oncall for sev1.
- Secondary owners: serving-runtime and infra-networks.

Definitions and degradation tiers:
- Tier 0 (Normal): All systems healthy.
- Tier 1 (Soft Degradation): Sustained elevated latency or queueing detected; soft feature degradation allowed (e.g., lower model temperature, shorter max tokens).
- Tier 2 (Aggressive Degradation): Backpressure across GPU pools or API queue length above threshold; non-critical routes should be shed and cache-hit routing prioritized.
- Tier 3 (Fallback/Regional Failover): Large-scale capacity loss; route to alternate region or downgrade to CPU-safe model variant with documented quality delta.

Detection signals (example metrics):
- ingress_request_queue_length (Gauge) > 500 for > 2m -> Tier 1 candidate
- model_variant_latency_p95 > 2x baseline for 3m -> Tier 1 -> Tier 2 escalation if sustained 10m
- gpu_utilization_all_p95 > 95% for 5m and pending_jobs > 100 -> Tier 2
- error_rate_5m > 0.5% or sustained 0.2% with increasing trend -> investigate for faults

Alerting thresholds (Prometheus-style suggested rules):
- ALERT HighIngressQueueLength
  IF ingress_request_queue_length > 500
  FOR 2m
  LABELS {severity="page"}
  ANNOTATIONS {summary="Ingress queue length > 500"}

- ALERT ModelLatencySpike
  IF increase(model_variant_latency_p95[5m]) > 100
  FOR 3m
  LABELS {severity="ticket"}

Dashboards (panel suggestions):
- Traffic Overview: total QPS, 1m/5m/15m, incoming error rates, top 10 routes by latency.
- Queueing & Backpressure: ingress_request_queue_length, per-node backlog, headroom by GPU pool.
- Cost vs Quality: token spend rate, average model size per request, fallback invocation count.
- Degradation State: current tier, active policies, recent automated actions.

Automated mitigation patterns (ordered from least to most disruptive):
1) Router-level smoothing: enforce concurrency limits per client key and apply token rate limiting.
2) Short-circuit caching: lookup prefix cache; return cached responses for frequent prompts with TTL < 5m policies.
3) Soft-quality degradations: reduce max_tokens, lower sampling temperature, disable non-essential plugins/tools for requests marked non-critical.
4) Model variant substitution: switch to a lower-cost quantized model variant pinned as compatible in the catalog (see model-onboarding policy).
5) Traffic shedding: deprioritize or 429 low-priority routes (background jobs, analytics).
6) Cross-region failover: route traffic to alternate region with capacity headroom.
7) Graceful denial mode: enable maintenance page or controlled error responses for affected customers with high QPS.

Automated action configuration examples (Envoy-like routing rules):
- Example: route-weight override to prefer cached backend:
  routes:
    - match: {prefix: "/v1/generate"}
      actions:
        - weighted_cluster: {clusters: [{name: model-cache, weight: 80}, {name: model-proxy, weight: 20}]}

- Example: rate limit by API key (YAML):
  rate_limits:
    - key: api_key
      limit: 100r/s
      burst: 200

Runbook: immediate response (Tier 1) - Step-by-step
1) Triage - Confirm alert details and affected routes (5 minutes).
   - Query: sum(rate(http_requests_total[1m])) by (route,api_key)
2) Short-term mitigation (5–10 minutes):
   - Apply router smoothing: lower concurrency per client to 8 requests.
   - Enable short-circuit cache lookup for top-5 heavy prompts (via feature-flag).
3) Evaluate impact (10–20 minutes):
   - Monitor p95 latency, queue length, error rate for 10 minutes.
   - If p95 latency falls < 1.5x baseline and error rate stable -> scale down mitigations gradually.
4) Escalate to Tier 2 if queueing or GPU saturation persists beyond 15 minutes.

Runbook: aggressive response (Tier 2)
1) Notify platform-sre and serving-runtime channel.
2) Trigger model variant substitution via deployment API (example):
   curl -X POST https://deploy.redwood.internal/api/v1/replace-variant -H "Authorization: Bearer $DEPLOY_TOKEN" -d '{"route": "/v1/generate","from": "gpt-large-fp16","to": "gpt-large-8bit-q"}'
3) Immediately enable traffic shedding for low-priority clients (set header X-Client-Priority).
4) Open ticket against cloud-provider capacity team if cross-region burst capacity is required.

Fallback choreography and customer impact communication:
- Maintain a small matrix of feature -> acceptable degradation steps for each critical product route. Example: chat-frontend -> reduce max_tokens then model-variant substitute -> notify customers via status page.
- Communicate via status.redwood.com and automated customer emails if customer SLA is affected beyond 30 minutes.

Testing and verification plan:
- Monthly chaos tests that simulate: queue buildup, GPU pool loss, regional network partition.
- Game day scenarios: 10-minute Tier 2 exercise run with telemetry capture and postmortem.
- Integration tests for automated variant switches: validate compatibility and latency regression < 20% for degraded variant.

Metrics to track post-incident (KPI):
- Time to detect (TTD) - goal < 2 minutes for high-severity signals.
- Time to first mitigation (TTM) - goal < 5 minutes.
- Time to recovery (TTR) - goal < 30 minutes for Tier 1, < 2 hours for Tier 2.
- Customer-facing errors during event (count).

Post-incident workflow and retrospective template:
1) Create incident ticket and assign notes: triggers, timeline, actions taken, automated switches.
2) Run standard postmortem within 72 hours: map root cause, gaps in detection, if thresholds were too noisy.
3) Action items: tune alert thresholds, add dashboard panels, update degradation matrix for affected routes.

Rollout checklist for adopting teams (minimal set):
- Add service-specific entries to the degradation matrix with owner approval.
- Implement router-side flags to allow short-circuit caching and quality toggles.
- Add alert rules and dashboard panels from the examples above.
- Perform one canary chaos exercise with platform support.

Appendices:
A) Sample Prometheus alert rule (YAML):
  groups:
  - name: platform-traffic.rules
    rules:
    - alert: IngressRequestQueueHigh
      expr: ingress_request_queue_length > 500
      for: 2m
      labels:
        severity: page
      annotations:
        summary: "Ingress queue length exceeding 500 for >2m"

B) Policy table (text):
  | Route Type       | Priority | Degradation Steps (order)                   | Contact Team |
  |------------------|----------|---------------------------------------------|--------------|
  | Customer API     | High     | Router smoothing, cache, variant-substitute | serving-runtime |
  | Admin/Backfill   | Low      | Immediate shedding (429)                    | infra-batch  |

C) Example CLI: check queue + switch variant:
  # view queue
  rlqctl list --pool api-ingress --min-age 60
  # switch variant
  deployctl replace-variant --route /v1/generate --to gpt-large-8bit-q
